To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IRE sequence is a central component of a larger interactional structure that is used by teachers to review student performance.

(a) the IRE sequence, which is the primary means through which teachers and students interact in classrooms, can be analyzed as a component of larger speech events and (b) the larger speech event of a quiz review is a means of public display of student performance on a written text.
the IRE sequence is a complex and dynamic phenomenon which is embedded in the context of a classroom activity and which is itself an important context for student participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the social organization of talk and text are interwoven in the classroom.
the ways in which a classroom activity, the review, shapes the interactional sequences which occur within the review.
the ways in which the IRE sequence, and the surrounding conversational context, are used in classroom interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this analysis of one speech event in a single classroom suggests the need to view the IRE sequence in the context of the classroom activity within which it is embedded and the need to view that classroom activity in terms of the social organization of school and the social organization of society.
the IRE sequence in this study is a complex interactional structure which is both embedded and constrained by the larger context of a quiz review.
IRE is a sequence which, when used in a quiz review, is embedded within a larger framework of teacher talk and is used to sanction student talk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classroom is a site for the construction of social identities, and that these identities are constructed through the interactional organization of classroom discourse.
the IRE sequence is an interactional resource for the teacher to display student performance, to provide feedback to students, and to manage the classroom.
the IRE sequence is not an independent unit but a part of a larger framework of teacher utterance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRE sequence is not simply a conversational structure but is instead a social and cultural practice.
IRE, and the classroom interactional sequences it supports, are not a simple and straightforward means of eliciting student responses.
the IRE sequence is a complex, multi-faceted, and dynamic social practice.
